newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: U.N. warns of troop build-up near Tajik capital.
newsitem.headline: U.N. warns of troop build-up near Tajik capital.

text.p: A senior United Nations official in war-ravaged Tajikistan said on Wednesday he was concerned about a build-up of government and opposition forces near the capital Dushanbe.

"We are a little bit worried to see there has been a certain build up of positions in the areas of Teppai-Samarkandi, Kofarnikhon and up to Nurek (all close to Dushanbe)," said Gerd Dietrich Merrem, the U.N. special representative in Tajikistan.

The reported build-up came only days before Tajikistan's secular government and the armed Islamist opposition are due to sign a peace agreement to end four years of civil war in the former Soviet republic.
"This does not help confidence," Merrem told reporters after meeting the Tajik President, Imomali Rakhmonov.
On Tuesday, the Tajik government said the signing of a final peace accord had been delayed until later this month for "technical reasons".
The conflict has killed tens of thousands and displaced many more in the remote, mountainous republic of 5.7 million people bordering Afghanistan and China.
A ceasefire brokered by the United Nations, Russia and Iran last December has largely held. The two sides have already agreed a power-sharing deal but some issues still have to be resolved.
